region: Sagaponack · The Hamptons, Long Island, New York
about: Wölffer Estate was founded in 1988 by Christian Wölffer, a Hamburg-born entrepreneur who had begun buying farmland in Sagaponack a decade earlier. Today his children, Marc and Joey Wölffer, own and run the estate, and Roman Roth, winemaker since 1992 and now a partner, leads the cellar. The vineyard lies about two and a half miles from the Atlantic, on the South Fork of Long Island.

The estate’s 55 acres of vines grow in Bridgehampton loam and are cooled by ocean breezes, conditions that favor a fresh, mineral style of Cabernet Franc rather than a heavy one. The wine is made and bottled at the estate in Sagaponack, and the winemaker’s notes point to fine toasted oak framing the fruit. The vineyard is certified by Long Island Sustainable Winegrowing.

The winemaker’s notes describe a dark brick-red wine with aromas of sandalwood, prunes, ripe blueberries and licorice, an elegant but firm palate with round fruit, minerality and ripe tannins, and a long finish with a hint of bell pepper, the classic signature of the grape. With a few years in bottle it has had time to soften and knit together.
